recommendedTextbook.title: A Guide to WASSCE/SSCE Literature-in-English
recommendedTextbook.author: Kola Eke
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: African Prose: Thematic Analysis of Prescribed WAEC Novel
subtopics: Prescribed African novel: Plot summary and chapter-by-chapter progression
Major themes: Colonial collision, cultural alienation, gender oppression, patriarchal hegemony, political betrayal
Stylistic techniques: Oral folklore motifs, proverbs, vernacular transliteration, symbolism
objectives: Write a coherent 400-word thematic essay on cultural conflict in the prescribed text
Analyze the narrative significance of 3 major symbolic motifs in the text
Assess how the author utilizes indigenous Nigerian idioms to enrich English prose

topics.topic: African Drama: Staging, Thematic Concerns and Character Dynamics
subtopics: Prescribed African play: Dramatic conflict, act/scene breakdown
Themes: Corruption in governance, traditional superstition vs modern medicine, youth revolt
Dramatic irony and tragic resolution in modern African theatre
objectives: Explain how the playwright uses dramatic irony to build audience suspense
Analyze the motivations and moral trajectory of the central antagonist
Examine stage directions and costume requirements for authentic African theatrical performance

topics.topic: African Poetry: Oral Heritage, Imagery and Poetic Voice
subtopics: Selected prescribed poems by African poets (e.g. Wole Soyinka, Gabriel Okara, Kofi Awoonor, Niyi Osundare)
Themes: Pan-Africanism, loss of ancestral culture, nature, poverty, lamentation
Poetic diction: Metaphorical language, musical rhythm, lyrical persona, stanzaic structure
objectives: Explicate the central theme and mood of a prescribed African poem
Identify sound and imagery devices that echo traditional African drum beats and laments
Compare the poetic voices of two West African poets addressing post-independence governance

topics.topic: Non-African Prose: Narrative Structure and Socio-Historical Context
subtopics: Prescribed Non-African novel: Industrial revolution, racial segregation, or totalitarian society context
Thematic exploration: Class stratification, racial prejudice, moral integrity, human dignity
Character evolution: Dynamic vs static character arcs, psychological realism
objectives: Contextualize the novel within its specific 19th/20th century historical epoch
Analyze character transformation through major ethical dilemmas in the narrative
Write an argumentative essay comparing social inequality in the text with contemporary societies
